The next email finding tool in the list is [GetProspect](https://getprospect.com/), which I primarily use to find emails at scale. GetProspect is really useful when you want to find emails from names, companies, domains, or LinkedIn profiles.

GetProspect gives access to a large B2B database. It covers **200M+ B2B contacts, 230M+ corporate emails, and 26M+ companies** worldwide. That’s great, right?

Basically, I start by searching emails using a person’s full name and company. This works perfectly when I already know who I want to contact.

![Getprospect Email Finder](<Base64-Image-Removed>)GetProspect Email Finder

GetProspect also supports **domain-based email search**. As a result, I can enter a company domain and view available business email addresses.

LinkedIn support is available through a **Chrome extension**. It helps get emails and enrich contact data while browsing profiles or lists.

_**Compliance:** GDPR compliant_

_**Best For:** Teams wanting bulk email finding with verification and enrichment_

Not only that, email accuracy is a key part of the workflow. GetProspect verifies emails in real time and claims credit refunds for invalid data.

It even offers bulk email finding for larger lists. This way, I can save and export thousands of contacts without manual cleanup.

GetProspect also offers b **ulk email verification**. This helps clean lists before sending cold email campaigns.

Next, while checking this email finder tool, I also used its data enrichment. It appends details like job title, location, industry, and technologies.

Overall, GetProspect feels built for structured email finding. I use it when I want verified emails with enrichment in one place.

#### Pros

- The accuracy of the email addresses is good
- You get advanced filters to find email addresses
- Team collaboration features included
- Real-time email verification included
- Bulk email finder and enrichment support
- Data enrichment to get additional contact information
- Chrome extension to find emails from LinkedIn

#### Cons

- The interface is complex and not easy to use
- Free credits are limited
- Cold email features may feel unnecessary for email-only use cases

#### Pricing (Billed Annually)

GetProspect offers three plans to its customers.

- **Free plan** with 600 email credits
- **Starter plan** with $34/month with 1,000 email credits
- **Growth plan** with $69/month with 5,000 email credits

**_Final Verdict:_** In my experience, GetProspect works well for bulk email finding with verification. If you want emails plus enrichment without using multiple tools, it fits that need.

### 8\. UpLead

**Accuracy:** 95% \| **Free Trial:** Available \| **Ease of Use:** 4.4/5

[UpLead](https://www.uplead.com/) helps when I want verified emails and do not want to pay for bad data. I rely on it to find emails using company names or website URLs.

UpLead lets me find emails by company name or website URL. I can also add a contact name to get a specific business email address.

The platform gives access to **180M+ B2B contacts**. This helps when building lists across different industries and regions.

_**Compliance:** GDPR and CCPA compliant_

_**Best For:** Teams wanting verified emails by company or domain_

Email verification runs in real time. UpLead flags accept-all and catch-all emails before export.

The best part? I pay only for valid emails. If there is no match, it does not consume credits.

UpLead also provides bulk email lookups. I just need to upload names and companies and get emails with extra details.

Along with emails, I also get phone numbers and social links. This adds context, but email finding remains the main aim.

Data accuracy stays consistent across searches. The 95% accuracy guarantee adds confidence before outreach.

Overall, UpLead fits structured email finding workflows. I use it when I want verified emails without guessing patterns.

#### Pros

- Real-time email verification
- Native CRM integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, and more
- The user interface is easy and quick to use
- Pay only for valid emails
- You will find limited data for niche markets
- Bulk email lookup service is supported

#### Cons

- Free trial is limited
- No credit rollover if you don’t use them
- The interface feels heavy for quick email finding

#### Pricing (Billed Annually)

UpLead offers four plans to its customers.

- **Free trial** for 7 days with five valid credits
- **Essential plan** with $99/month with 170 credits
- **Plus plan** with $199/month with 400 credits
- **Professional plan** with a custom quote

**_Final Verdict:_** In my experience, UpLead works well when email accuracy is non-negotiable. If you want verified emails without paying for guesses, it fits that need.

### 9\. Findymail

**Accuracy:** 90% \| **Free Trial:** 10 finder credits \| **Ease of Use:** 4.6/5

Next in the list is [Findymail](https://www.findymail.com/), which I review mainly for one reason. It allows you to find verified and bounce-free email addresses without wasting credits.

All I have to do is enter a person’s name and company domain. In most cases, FindyMail returns a verified business email directly.

What stands out is how billing works. FindyMail charges only for valid emails, not duplicates or failed results.

![Findymail Email Finder](<Base64-Image-Removed>)Findymail Email Finder

This matters when running cold email campaigns at scale. I do not lose credits on emails I cannot use.

Email verification is built into the core workflow. FindyMail guarantees less than 5% invalid emails, and my tests stayed below 2%.

_**Compliance:** GDPR compliant_

_**Best For:** Teams wanting verified emails without paying for invalid results_

I do not need to re-verify emails using another tool. That saves both time and cost during outreach setup.

FindyMail also supports bulk email finding, which is super helpful when you have a large list of emails. This helps you to get the email addresses of a bulk of your prospects without much hassle.

Plus, FindyMail offers email enrichment. It helps to update CRM data without extra steps. That’s not all.

You can even use AI to find email addresses, which makes the entire process easy and quick, as you just need to type a prompt.

Overall, FindyMail feels built for cold email deliverability. I use it when I want clean emails without paying for unusable data.

#### Pros

- Guaranteed less than 5% bounce rate
- Pay only for valid email results
- Built-in email verification
- FindyMail integrates with LinkedIn Sales Navigator and Apollo Data Scraper
- Bulk email finding and enrichment support
- Unused credits roll over

#### Cons

- No free forever plan
- Support response can slow down during peak times

#### Pricing

It comes with a pay-as-you-go pricing model.

- **Free Trial:** 10 finder + 10 verifier credits (one-time)
- **Starter:** $41/month (billed annually)
- 1,000 finder credits
- 1,000 email verification credits

**_Final Verdict:_** In my experience, FindyMail works best when deliverability is non-negotiable. If you want verified emails without paying for bad data, it is a strong choice.

> You can also read our guide on [top email scraping tools](https://www.saleshandy.com/blog/email-scraping-tools/) to find accurate email addresses.

### 10\. Skrapp.io

**Accuracy:** 93% \| **Free Credits:** Limited \| **Ease of Use:** 4.5/5

Next in the list is [Skrapp.io](https://skrapp.io/), which I check mainly for finding business email addresses. The platform allows me to get email addresses from a name, a company name, or a company website.

To find emails, I begin by entering a full name and company. Skrapp returns business emails that I can review before outreach.

![Skrapp.io Email Finder](<Base64-Image-Removed>)Skrapp.io Email Finder

It also supports company-based email search. I enter a company name or website and see available professional emails.

_**Compliance:** GDPR and CCPA compliant_

_**Best For:** Sales, marketing, or BDR teams wanting simple email finding without extra steps_

I also explored Skrapp’s integration with **LinkedIn and Sales Navigator**. I can find anyone’s email while browsing profiles without switching tabs.

The next important thing is email verification. Skrapp runs email verification during email search. So, I only get the emails that are valid and safe for cold email outreach.

You also have the option to use **bulk email finding**, supporting CSV or Excel uploads if you already have a large contact list.

The platform also offers an **Email Finder API**. This helps when email finding needs to run inside another workflow. The interface stays easy to follow during searches.

It makes it easy to find emails without setting up rules or filters. Overall, Skrapp is best for email finding. I use it to verify email addresses associated with names, companies, or LinkedIn profiles.

#### Pros

- Find emails by name and company
- Company email revealer is supported
- Real-time email verification
- LinkedIn and Sales Navigator support
- Bulk email finder and API access
- Native integrations with Salesforce, Outreach, and Zoho

#### Cons

- Free usage is limited
- Sometimes the platform is buggy
- Bulk email search doesn’t remove invalid and catch-all email addresses

#### Pricing (Billed Annually)

Skrapp offers three plans to its customers.

- **Free plan** with 100 email credits per month
- **Professional plan** with $18 per month, with 1000 email credits/month
- **Enterprise plan** with $157 per month, with 50,000 email credits/month

**_Final Verdict:_** In my experience, Skrapp.io works well for direct email finding tasks. If the goal is to get business emails without added layers, it fits well.

For emails sourced specifically from LinkedIn profiles, you may also want to read our guide on [LinkedIn email finder tools](https://www.saleshandy.com/blog/linkedin-email-finder/).

### 11\. Snov.io

**Accuracy:** 75–79% \| **Free Credits:** 50/month \| **Ease of Use:** 4.0/5

[Snov.io](http://snov.io/)  shows up in almost every email finder discussion, and for good reason.

It packs email finding, verification, drip campaigns, and a basic CRM into one platform. For teams that want to consolidate tools on a smaller budget, it is worth looking at.

The email finder searches a database of 50M+ company profiles using 15 filters.

You can also look up emails by name and domain, pull contacts from LinkedIn with their Chrome extension, or upload CSVs for bulk searches.

I tested it with my standard 100-contact list, and Snov.io found verified emails for 79 out of 100 contacts. That is below most other tools here, but the ones it found were generally usable.

One pattern I noticed — Snov.io works better for mid-to-large companies.

![Snov is the best email lookup tool](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

When I searched for contacts at smaller firms or niche industries, the hit rate dropped. The database does not include phone numbers either, so if you need both emails and direct dials, this is not the right pick.

The verification side is solid.

Snov.io runs a 7-tier check covering syntax, MX records, SMTP responses, and disposable email detection.

When it marks an email as “valid,” I can trust it more than some tools that just guess patterns and hope for the best.

#### Pros

- All in one setup: finding, verification, campaigns, and CRM in one tool
- Free trial renews every 30 days for ongoing light testing
- Verification system is thorough and reliable
- Bulk domain search can process up to 20,000 domains at once
- Integrates with 5,000+ apps through Zapier

#### Cons

- Accuracy is lower than most tools on this list
- Database lacks phone numbers entirely
- Credits are shared between finder and verifier, so verification reduces search quota
- Starter plan is restrictive with limited warm up slots and no A B testing
- LinkedIn automation costs extra per account
- UI can feel cluttered for first time users

#### Pricing

- Trial: Free (50 credits/month, 100 recipients/month) — renewable but limited
- Starter: $39/month (1,000 credits, 5,000 recipients)
- Pro S: $74.25/month (5,000 credits, 25,000 recipients)
- LinkedIn automation: +$69/month per slot (separate from all plans)

All prices reflect annual billing.

#### _Final Verdict_

Snov.io is a reasonable all-in-one option if your outreach volume stays low and you want email finding plus campaigns in one workspace. The verification is solid, and the renewable free trial is useful for testing.

### 12\. RocketReach

**Accuracy:** 82–85% \| **Free Credits:** 5/month \| **Ease of Use:** 4.2/5

[RocketReach](https://rocketreach.co/) has a strong reputation in recruiting and enterprise sales. The main draw is getting email addresses and direct dial phone numbers from the same lookup — something most standalone email finders do not offer.

The database covers 700M+ professional profiles across 35M+ companies. You can search by name, company, title, location, and industry.

The tool returns both professional and personal emails when available, which is particularly useful for recruiting and C-level outreach where a work email alone may not get through.

I ran the same 100-contact test. RocketReach returned results for 82 contacts, but some came back flagged as “likely” rather than “verified.”

When I filtered strictly for verified emails, the usable count was closer to 78-80. That is mid-range for this list — better than Snov.io, but noticeably behind the top performers.

![RocketReach a B2B data provider](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

The phone number data is where RocketReach justifies its higher price. If you need direct dials alongside email addresses, this is one of the better options available.

Many email finder tools either skip phone data entirely or hide it behind expensive enterprise tiers. RocketReach makes it a core part of the offering, though the per-credit cost reflects that.

Bulk lookups work through CSV uploads, and the API is solid for teams automating enrichment workflows.

Exports come back clean and structured. But there is no outreach functionality — RocketReach is purely a data tool. You find contacts, export them, and take them somewhere else to actually run campaigns.

#### Pros

- Strong phone number coverage alongside emails
- Returns personal emails, useful for recruiting and executive outreach
- Broad coverage across industries and company sizes
- Clean bulk exports and a solid API for enrichment workflows
- Chrome extension works on LinkedIn and company websites

#### Cons

- Expensive compared to most tools on this list
- Users report higher bounce rates on some searches
- No outreach, campaign, or CRM functionality
- Credits do not roll over, unused lookups expire monthly
- Only 5 free lookups, not enough for a proper test
- Accuracy is inconsistent across company sizes and industries

#### Pricing

- Essentials: $69/month (100 lookups/month, email only)
- Pro: $119/month (250 lookups/month, email + phone)
- Ultimate: $249/month (500 lookups/month, email + phone + API)

All plans billed annually. No free trial — just 5 free lookups.

#### _Final Verdict_

RocketReach makes sense if your primary need is phone numbers and personal emails alongside work addresses.

For recruiting, executive outreach, and account-based sales, the data coverage is broad and the phone number quality is above average.

But the cost per lookup is high, accuracy does not match the top tools here, and there is zero outreach functionality.

## FAQs About Email Finding Tools

### 1\. How can you choose the right email finder tool?

Choosing the right email finder depends on how you plan to use it. Start by checking the accuracy rate, since verified emails reduce bounce issues. Then look at ease of use, as some tools are simpler than others.

Also, review the features you need, such as bulk email finding, LinkedIn support, or CRM integrations. Finally, compare pricing plans and ensure they match your budget and usage needs.

### 2\. Is there a free way to look up an email address?

Yes, some tools allow limited free email lookups. Platforms like Saleshandy Lead Finder and AnyMail Finder provide free searches with restrictions. Many paid tools also offer free credits or trials, which help test accuracy before upgrading.

### 3\. Are email finder tools legal to use?

Yes, email finder tools are legal when used for legitimate business purposes. You should focus on work email addresses, keep outreach relevant, and include an unsubscribe option. Using these tools for spamming or misuse can be unethical and illegal.

### 4\. Is there an AI tool for finding emails?

Yes, some tools use AI to speed up email discovery. For example, Saleshandy’s AI Lead Finder lets you type a simple prompt and get verified leads. This helps build prospect lists faster with less manual work.

### 5\. What features should you look for in an email finder tool?

Important features include email verification, bulk email finding, and data accuracy. Integrations with CRMs, APIs, and automation tools can also be useful. The goal is to remove guesswork and ensure the emails you find are usable.

### 6\. How do email finder tools work?

Email finder tools collect data from public sources like websites, company pages, directories, and social platforms. They use pattern matching and domain analysis to predict email formats.

Modern tools also use AI and verification checks to confirm accuracy and reduce bounces.

## How to Migrate from Hunter.io Without Losing Data

If you decide to move away from Hunter.io, the transition doesn’t have to be disruptive. Here’s a simple migration framework to help you switch tools while maintaining your prospecting performance and data integrity.

### Step 1: Export Your Data from Hunter.io

- Log into your Hunter.io dashboard
- Navigate to **Campaigns** \> **Lists** and export all saved lists
- Download your email verification history if needed
- Export any custom tags or notes you’ve added
- Save your domain search results and leads
- Document your most successful prospecting workflows

### Step 2: Clean & Organize Your Data

- Remove duplicate contacts from your exported lists
- Verify and update outdated contact information
- Segment your highest-performing contact lists for priority migration
- Standardize field names and data formats (CSV cleanup)
- Create a backup of all exported data
- Tag contacts by campaign or source for easier organization

### Step 3: Choose Your New Platform

- Based on the quiz above, select 2-3 alternatives that match your use case
- Start free trials simultaneously to compare performance
- Test with a small batch of contacts first (50-100)
- Evaluate data accuracy, deliverability, and user experience
- Consider integration requirements with existing tools

### Step 4: Set Up Your New Platform

- Create your account and configure basic settings
- Import your cleaned contact lists using CSV upload
- Set up CRM integrations (HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive)
- Configure Chrome extensions and browser tools
- Connect email accounts for sequencing (if applicable)
- Set up team members and permissions

### Step 5: Reconnect Integrations

- Update your **Zapier** zaps if you were using Hunter.io webhooks
- Reconnect **CRM workflows** and data syncs
- Install new **Chrome extensions**
- Set up **Gmail/Outlook** connections for email sequences
- Update any API integrations in your stack
- Test all integrations with sample data

### Step 6: Configure Email Settings (If Switching to Automation Tools)

If moving to **Snov.io** or **Saleshandy**:

- Enable email warm-up features immediately
- Configure inbox rotation for multiple sending accounts
- Set up SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records
- Start with low sending volumes and gradually increase
- Monitor deliverability metrics closely

### Step 7: Run Parallel Campaigns (Week 1-2)

- Keep Hunter.io active during initial testing period
- Run small test campaigns with your new tool (50-100 contacts)
- Compare deliverability, open rates, and response rates
- Ensure data accuracy meets your standards
- Validate that integrations work correctly

### Step 8: Monitor Performance Metrics

Track these KPIs for 2 weeks before full migration:

- **Email bounce rate** (should be <5%)
- **Open rate** (benchmark against Hunter.io campaigns)
- **Reply rate** (quality indicator)
- **Data accuracy** (% of valid emails)
- **Cost per verified lead** (ROI calculation)
- **Time saved** (efficiency gains)

### Step 9: Full Migration

Once confident in your new tool:

- Cancel your Hunter.io subscription (or downgrade to free plan as backup)
- Migrate all remaining contact lists
- Update all team documentation and training materials
- Announce the change to your team with clear instructions
- Archive Hunter.io data for historical reference

### Step 10: Optimize and Scale

After migration:

- Refine your new workflows based on initial results
- Scale up your prospecting volume gradually
- Train team members on advanced features
- Set up reporting dashboards
- Document best practices for your specific use case

### Pro Tips:

✅ **Keep Hunter.io’s free plan** (25 searches) as backup for quick verifications

✅ **Overlap subscriptions** for 2-3 weeks to ensure smooth transition

✅ **Use email verification tools** to clean exported data before import

✅ **Set up parallel prospecting** to test new platform performance

✅ **Document new workflows** for team training and consistency

✅ **Start with one user** before rolling out team-wide

✅ **Export historical data** from Hunter.io for future reference

## Final Thoughts: Choosing the Best Hunter.io Alternative for Your Business

Hunter.io isn’t necessarily _bad_, it’s excellent at what it does (email verification). The question is: **Is that enough for your needs?**

If you only need email finding and verification, Hunter.io remains a solid choice. But if you need prospecting automation, better data coverage, or more complete sales workflows, the alternatives above will serve you better.

## FAQs: Hunter.io Alternatives

**Should I export my Hunter.io data before switching?**

Absolutely. Migration is the perfect time to clean your contact lists. Export all your Hunter.io lists, verification history, and saved searches before switching. Use the new platform’s verification features to clean this data before importing. This removes outdated contacts and improves deliverability from day one. Starting fresh with verified data helps your new platform build better performance and avoids the bounce rate issues that often plague migrations.

**Which Hunter.io alternative has the best data accuracy?**

**UpLead** offers the best data accuracy among Hunter.io alternatives with a 95%+ guarantee and pay-only-for-verified model. **ZoomInfo** also provides excellent accuracy for enterprise use. Both consistently outperform Hunter.io’s verification rates according to user reviews. UpLead is particularly strong because they only charge credits for verified, accurate contacts—not guesses.

**Can I use Hunter.io alongside another tool?**

Yes, many teams use specialized tools in combination. For example, Hunter.io for verification + Saleshandy for email sequences, or Hunter.io for domain searches + Apollo.io for CRM. However, this creates workflow complexity and extra costs. Most teams get better results choosing one comprehensive platform like Apollo.io or Snov.io that handles finding, verification, and outreach rather than juggling multiple disconnected tools.

**Is Apollo.io better than Hunter.io for B2B prospecting?**

**Apollo.io vs Hunter.io** shows Apollo winning for all-in-one functionality with its 275M+ contact database, built-in CRM, and native email sequences. Hunter.io focuses purely on email finding/verification. Apollo provides better value for teams wanting prospecting + outreach in one platform at a similar price point. However, Hunter.io remains simpler and more specialized if you only need email verification without automation.

**Will switching from Hunter.io disrupt my workflow?**

Not if you plan properly. Keep Hunter.io active (even just the free 25 searches) while you set up and test your new platform. Import your contact lists and run small test campaigns first. Most alternatives accept CSV imports from Hunter.io, making the transition smooth. Teams complete migrations without losing momentum by running both platforms in parallel for 1-2 weeks until confident in the new tool.

**What Hunter.io competitors offer cold email automation**?

**Saleshandy**, **Snov.io**, **Apollo.io**, and **VoilaNorbert** all offer native cold email automation—something Hunter.io lacks entirely. Saleshandy ($27/mo) specializes in deliverability with email warm-up features. Snov.io ($39/mo) provides the most affordable all-in-one solution. Apollo.io includes automation as part of a complete sales platform. Hunter.io requires external tools like Lemlist or Smartlead for campaigns.

**What’s the biggest mistake teams make when switching from Hunter.io?**

Assuming all tools work the same way. Hunter.io is purely a data tool, while alternatives like Apollo.io and Snov.io are complete platforms. Teams jump into the new tool trying to use it exactly like Hunter.io and miss powerful features. Spend 2-3 hours exploring your new platform’s capabilities—especially automation, enrichment, and integration features that Hunter.io doesn’t offer. This learning investment pays off quickly in productivity gains.
